the change in collection frequency did not significantly alter the recycling performance indicators and that the change in recycling performance indicators was not significantly altered by the change in collection regime.
the change in collection frequency from 2 weeks to 4 weeks had no effect on the recycling behaviour of the community as a whole.
The impact of a change in collection frequency on the recycling behaviour of households in the study area is minimal.

the impact of a change in collection frequency of a newspaper recycling scheme on the recycling performance of the participating community.
the behaviour of households and the impact on their recycling activity of changing the collection frequency of kerbside recycling schemes.
understanding how the performance of a kerbsiderecycling scheme is affected by changing the collection frequency.

the intervention did not affect recycling behaviour.

, although there was no change in recycling performance, the intervention did not have a significant impact on the recycling behaviours of the community, but it may have had a small impact on a minority of the population.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kerbside newspaper scheme was robust enough to withstand a change in collection frequency without a significant loss of participation.
the kerbside collection of newspapers can be made more cost-effective, without significantly compromising the performance of the service.
recycling is a complex behaviour, and that it is difficult to make predictions on its future performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recycling performance indicators are not necessarily good indicators of the underlying recycling behaviours of the community.
it is important to understand the underlying behaviour of households before undertaking changes to recycling regimes.
the collection frequency is not the most significant factor in determining the success or failure of kerbside newspaper schemes.
